At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time there was a bhikṣu named Sāti,
who was young and had recently gone forth.
Not long after he had received full ordination,
while he was first studying the Vinaya, he gathered reeds for the community to use as a bathing mat.
A black snake entered a hole in the reeds and bit his right big toe.
Poison attacked his body; he fell to the ground, spat foam, and rolled his eyes upward in a wild gaze.
Seeing his suffering, Ānanda went to where the Buddha was and reported all of this to the Buddha in detail.
"How should one treat and rescue them?
The Buddha told Ānanda, "Retain my words;
employ the Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī mantra to eliminate evil poisons."
Go there to gather them in and protect them,
so that the body of the bhikṣu Sāti may attain peace and happiness.

You should establish a boundary against devas, nāgas, asuras, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, pīlitas, piśācas, bhūtas, kūṣmāṇḍas, pūtanas, śakatas, ūrmadās, caryas, apasmāras, uttarakauravas, yātudhānas, aupadhikas, bhadras, and those who cannot be commanded.
Improper diet, foul spittle, evil shadows, evil sights,
evil writings, evil crossings, and evil belching;
[fevers] lasting one day, two days, three days, or four days.
Extending even to seven days, half a month, or a full month;
whether for a brief moment or for a long duration;
characterized by alternating cold and heat, wind, cold, phlegm, and catarrh.
Some may suffer from the three ailments of cold, heat, and headache;
may they all be cured and relieved.
Others may suffer from a partial headache or an inability to eat.
Pain in the eyes, nose, ears, and mouth;
pain in the heart, head, and cheeks; pain in the throat and pharynx;
and wind in the teeth, heart, chest, ribs, back, and abdomen.

May the wind-diseases of the spleen and calves, the wind-diseases of the hands and feet, and the wind-diseases of the bones and joints— by the supernatural power of the Buddha and through this vow— be eliminated from the body of [Name],
so that they may be peaceful, secure, and happy day and night.
Thus is the recitation of the mantra.

By means of the Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī,
whether entering a kingdom or reaching an araṇya,
whether on the right path or a wrong path, or approaching a royal palace.
In the face of bandits, strife, water, fire, enmity, and malice;
when among great crowds, or bitten by snakes, or having consumed poison—
one should, in all instances of fear, recollect this mantra.
If wind, phlegm, cold, or heat combine,
one should likewise bring them to mind when afflicted by any of the four hundred and four diseases; furthermore,
if unintentional suffering should arise, one should also bring it to mind.
For what reason? Ānanda, if a person is destined to be imprisoned, they may be released by means of a fine;
if they are destined for flogging, they may be released by means of a beating with a staff.
If one should be liberated through being struck with a staff or a blow to the ear;
if one should be liberated through a blow to the ear and harsh abuse;
or if one should be liberated through harsh abuse and admonition.
If one should be admonished, it does not involve verbal liberation.
Such liberation is free from all illness.
Ānanda, among gods, humans, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas, I do not see anyone [who can surpass this].
For those who are protected and guarded by this Great Peacock King Dhāraṇī,
there shall be peace and security, and the poison of punishment shall be eliminated;
when they bind the boundary and the ground, none shall dare to approach to cause them fear.
Whether it be devas, or the parents of devas, or the hosts of deva sons and daughters;
or nāgas, or the parents of nāgas, or the nāga sons, daughters, and hosts;
or asuras, or the parents of asuras, or the asura sons, daughters, and hosts.

or the Gandharvas and the assemblies of their parents, children, and kin;

If devas and others obtain the human expedient means,

Because these [deities] have appeared before that host of devas,

Vipaśyin Buddha relied upon the aśoka tree;

The Gautama Śākyamuni Buddha attained enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree;
regarding the great supernormal powers of all Buddhas, [he is unsurpassed].
When they have faith in the various devas,
those devas will all rejoice greatly;
may they always wish for their peace and security— such is this mantra.

*Hare hareṇi, care careṇi, paramaṇi, mohaṇi, saṃdhavaṇi, śāmbhaṇi, svāhā.* Ānanda, in the east is Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
He leads the Gandharva kings,
whose number exceeds ten million,
surrounding and guarding the Heavenly King of the East from before and behind.
Furthermore, there shall be children, grandchildren, brothers, as well as great ministers, military commanders, officials, and the masses of citizens, who,
by means of this Great Peacock King Dhāraṇī,
shall be protected, guarded, and watched over, remaining secure and joyful for a hundred years.

surrounding and protecting the Southern Heavenly King from all sides as he keeps watch.
Furthermore, may children, grandchildren, brothers, ministers, military commanders, officials, citizens, and the great assembly,
by means of this Great Peacock King Dhāraṇī,
be protected, guarded, and watched over, so that all may live for a hundred springs.

may they protect me so that I may see a hundred springs.

The yakṣa named Anupama resides in the country of Pāṭaliputra;

the yakṣa named Śaila resides in the country of Bhadra.

The yakṣa Kālotpala resides in the land of Vipula.
The yakṣa Citraratha dwells in the kingdom of Tiṅtiṅkuka.
The yakṣa Bakula possesses a great army and great power.
There are also the yakṣas Khanda and Upakhanda.

The yakṣa Kambalapaṭācara resides in the kingdom of Virā,
